newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 14.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet's package of measures for supporting the economy should include short-term exchange and budgetary measures, swift completion of privatisation, transparency of the capital and financial markets, new conditions for enterprise, support for exports, preservation of the Czech market and more concern for financial and economic criminality, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- Chairmen of Czech and Slovak Social Democratic Parties, Milos Zeman, Jaroslav Volf and Josef Migas, called on Prime Ministers Vaclav Klaus and Vladimir Meciar to not postpone a meeting.
- Czech Airlines (CSA) will most probably lose its subsidiary Slovak Air Services, because the company's employees will not be allowed to enter the Bratislava airport beginning in May.

- Ceska Sporitelna plans to increase its interest on deposits by 0.6 percent yearly. LIDOVE NOVINY - Hospitals with high unbalanced expenses should be financed by the government budget through health insurance companies, and the network of drug distributors should be restricted. Health Minister Jan Strasky decided to propose this for the cabinet's package of economic measures.
- President Vaclav Havel will not meet with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, whose visit to Prague was postponed until April 20. On that date, Havel will be in the Netherlands.

- Foreign Minister Joseef Zieleniec met with his Paraguayan counterpart, Ruben Lanzon, and signed a mutual trade agreement over the weekend. MLADA FRONTA DNES - Reports vary on the exact number of teachers who protested for higher wages on Old Town Square in Prague on Saturday. The police agreed on 6,000, while the union spoke of 14,000 participants.
- Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec travelled to the United States yesterday, where he will meet with his counterpart Madeleine Albright and with other representatives about expanding NATO.

- Evropska Banka made an agreement with Slovak representatives to sell its share in Slovonaft to the Slovak National Property Fund. PRAVO - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Nova television yesterday that the Czech economy is not in a crisis, but only in a short-term slump.

- In March, the highest year-on-year price increase was in construction (10.9 percent). The lowest price increase was in agricultural products (1.9 percent), according to the Czech Statistical Bureau.
